THALABI:v6p242/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p242/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p242/r6.claim: God reassures Moses and says He will return the serpent to its former form as a staff.
THALABI:v6p242/r6.anchor: سنُعيدها سيرتها أي إلى سيرتها وهيئتها الأولى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p22/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p22/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p22/r1.claim: Fear of a snake is natural; Moses feared because the staff he could use to kill it had itself become a snake, and God reassured him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p22/r1.anchor: Moses (sws) was scared because he thought that the staff he could use to kill the snake with had itself become a snake.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r7.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r7.claim: Makkī’s account says God had to command Moses to take the snake repeatedly before he obeyed on the third command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r7.anchor: ويبعد ما ذكره مكي في تفسيره أنه قيل له خذ مرة وثانية حتى قيل له خذها ولا تخف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r8.claim: He rejects Makkī’s account as unfitting for a prophet to disobey his Lord’s command twice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r8.anchor: لأن منصب النبوة لا يليق أن يأمره ربه مرة وثانية فلا يمتثل ما أمر به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r9.claim: Once Moses took the serpent in his hand, it became a staff again; سيرة comes from walking and extends to mean a way or manner, as the cited poem illustrates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r9.anchor: وحين أخذها بيده صارت عصا والسيرة من السير كالركبة والجلسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r10.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r10.claim: Al-Ḥawfī parses سيرتها as a second object of سنعيدها with an omitted preposition, or as a substitute for the object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r10.anchor: فقال الحوفي مفعول ثان لسنعيدها على حذف الجار مثل واختار موسى قومه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r11.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r11.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows سيرتها to substitute for the object as an explanation of its quality and manner.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses سيرتها as an adverb meaning in its former manner, when it was a staff; the author objects that this fixed adverb needs a preposition, omitted only rarely or poetically.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p323/r12.anchor: قال الزمخشري: يجوز أن ينتصب على الظرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p324/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p324/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p324/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also derives the construction from عاد بمعنى رجع إليه, which takes two objects; al-Ḥawfī had given this as his first analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p324/r1.anchor: وعادك أن تلاقيها عداء فيتعدى إلى مفعولين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p324/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p324/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p324/r2.claim: He prefers a third parse: سنعيدها stands independently for restoring the staff after it disappeared through transformation; سيرتها is an understood verbal clause, ‘moving along its former way.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p324/r2.anchor: ووجه ثالث حسن وهو أن يكون سنعيدها مستقلا بنفسه غير متعلق بسيرتها

SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r1.claim: One parse makes سيرتها an adverbial accusative, “in its former way.”
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r1.anchor: أن تكون منصوبة على الظرف أي: في سيرتها أي: طريقتها

SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r2.claim: The Shaykh objects that سيرتها is a specific adverb, normally unreachable by the verb without في except in anomalous usage.
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r2.anchor: إلا أن الشيخ رده بأنه ظرف مختص، ولا يصل إليه الفعل إلا بوساطة " في "

SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r3.claim: Another parse makes سيرتها an apposition of inclusion to ها in سنعيدها: restore it to its former attribute and shape.
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r3.anchor: أنها منصوبة على أنها بدل من ها " سنعيدها " بدل اشتمال؛ لأن السيرة الصفة أي: سنعيدها صفتها وشكلها

SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r4.claim: A third analysis supplies the dropped preposition إلى: restore it to its former way.
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r4.anchor: أنها منصوبة على إسقاط الخافض أي: إلى سيرتها

SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also parses it as a second object of عاده, “return to,” citing a line of Zuhayr.
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا، من عاده أي: عاد إليه، فيتعدى لمفعولين

SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r6.claim: Zuhayr's line عادك أن تلاقيها العداء supports عاده meaning “return to.”

SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r7.claim: سيرة is a form denoting the manner of السير, like ركبة from ركوب, then broadened to mean a way or practice.
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r7.anchor: والسيرة: فعلة تدل على الهيئة من السير كالركبة من الركوب، ثم اتسع فعبر بها عن المذهب والطريقة

SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r8.claim: Khalid al-Hudhali's verse uses سيرة in the sense of a way or practice.
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r8.anchor: فلا تغضبن من سيرة أنت سرتها

SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r9.claim: A final parse supplies يسير سيرتها الأولى and treats the clause as circumstantial: restore it while it follows its former course.
SAMIN-DURR:20:21/r9.anchor: ينتصب بفعل مضمر أي: يسير سيرتها الأولى، وتكون هذه الجملة المقدرة في محل نصب على الحال

ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r4.claim: سيرتها means its way or form; the staff will be restored to its former shape. Although sīra and ṭarīqa often mean actions, one says people share one form or resemblance.
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r4.anchor: معنى (سيرتها) طريقتها يعنى - هيئتها، تقول إذا كان القوم مشتبهين: هم على سيرة واحدة

ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r5.claim: سيرتها is accusative because the preposition إلى is omitted from سنعيدها إلى سيرتها الأولى, allowing the verb to govern it directly.
ZAJJAJ:v3p354/r5.anchor: و (سيرتها) منصوب على إسقاط الخافض، وأفضى الفعل إليها، المعنى - والله أعلم - سنعيدها

ASAD-NOTES:20:21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:21/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:21/r1.claim: God tells Moses to take the snake without fear and promises to restore the staff to its original state.
ASAD-NOTES:20:21/r1.anchor: Take hold of it, and fear not: We shall restore it to its former state

ASAD-NOTES:20:21#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:21#n14/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:21#n14/r1.claim: Asad reads the staff's transformation mystically as an allusion to appearance versus reality and the spiritual insight God grants chosen servants; Moses' encounter with the unnamed sage and the wording in 27:10 and 28:31 support this reading.
ASAD-NOTES:20:21#n14/r1.anchor: the staff into a serpent has, I believe, a mystic significance: it seems to be an allusion to the intrinsic difference between appearance and reality

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r1.claim: After stopping in reverence and returning in great fear, Moses is told to take the serpent; fear is a natural human response to such a sight and does not diminish prophetic rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r1.anchor: ولعل ذلك الخوف مما اقتضته الطبيعة البشرية فان البشر بمقتضى طبعه يخاف عند مشاهدة مثل ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the serpent was male.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r2.anchor: وكانت على ما روى عن ابن عباس ذكرا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r3.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r3.claim: Wahb reports that God specified that Moses take the serpent with his right hand.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r3.anchor: وعن وهب أنه تعالى قال له : ( خذها بيمينك )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r4.claim: One view explains Moses’ fear as a response to a terrifying event directly from God whose nature he had not yet understood; Abraham did not fear the fire because it came through God’s enemy and its nature was clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r4.anchor: إنما خاف عليه السلام لأنه رأى امرا هائلا صدر من الله عز وجل بلا واسطة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r5.claim: Another view says Moses feared because he knew that a member of this species had played a part in Adam’s expulsion from Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r5.anchor: لأنه عرف ما لقى من ذلك الجنس حيث كان له مدخل في خروج أبيه من الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r6.claim: Coordinating the prohibition with the command signals that not fearing is independently intended, rather than merely instrumental to taking the serpent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r6.anchor: وإنما عطف النهى على الأمر للاشعار بأن عدم المنهى عنه مقصود لذاته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r7.claim: After Moses takes it, God will restore the serpent to its former staff-state; that promise explains why Moses should obey and not fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r7.anchor: التي هي العصوية استئناف مسوق لتعليل الامتثال بالأمر والنهى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r8.claim: A proposed wisdom is that the transformation, command to take it, and prohibition of fear prepare Moses for what will happen with Pharaoh; al-Ālūsī says this may underlie the claim that the promise is a further reassurance and sign, though that reading is not clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r8.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن حكمة انقلابها حية وأمره باخذها ونهيه عن الخوف تانيسه فيما يعلم سبحانه أنه سيقع منه مع فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r9.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r9.claim: Aḥmad and others transmit from Wahb that Moses first covered his hand with his wool garment; an angel asked whether it would protect him if God allowed harm, Moses admitted his weakness, then put his hand in the serpent’s mouth and grasped its jaws; it became his familiar staff again. Al-Ālūsī says the account in which he directly takes it better suits prophetic dignity.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r9.anchor: في رواية الامام أحمد وغيره عن وهب أنه لما امره الله تعالى باخذها ادنى طرف المدرعة على يده

ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Moses was called to take it three times and only took it after the third call; Makkī says the third call included the promise to restore it. Al-Ālūsī finds this remote from prophetic dignity and suggests the report may be unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p177#4/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أنه عليه السلام نودى المرة الأولى يا موسى خذها فلم ياخذها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r1.claim: Sīra derives from travel and first meant the form or state of a journey, then broadened to a general manner or state; it can mean a way or school, as in the cited line about a manner one has followed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r1.anchor: والسيرة فعلة من السير تقال للهيءة والحالة الواقعة فيه ثم جردت لمطلق الهيئة والحالة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r2.speaker: الحوفى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r2.claim: Al-Ḥawfī’s analysis treats سِيرَتَهَا as a second object with a preposition omitted, originally إلى سيرتها or لسيرتها; Ibn Mālik adopts this analysis and Ibn Hishām approves it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r2.anchor: مفعول ثان لسنعيدها على حذف الجار نحو

ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r3.speaker: الزمخشرى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows اعاد from عاده, meaning “return to it,” to govern two objects directly; the cited line by Zuhayr uses عادك to mean “turned you away.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r3.anchor: بمعنى عاد اليه ومنه قول زهير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r4.speaker: الأصمعى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r4.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī and other lexicographers attest that عاد can take a direct object with the sense of turning or returning, supporting the transitive analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r4.anchor: نقل الطيبى عن الاصمعى أن عادك في البيت متعد بمعنى صرفك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r5.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ analyzes سِيرَتَهَا as an appositive of inclusion replacing the object pronoun in سنعيدها.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r5.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : هي بدل من ضمير المفعول بدل اشتمال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects treating سِيرَتَهَا as an adverbial accusative because a specific manner is not an indefinite adverbial; a preposition في is needed, and omission is only poetic or anomalous.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r6.anchor: وتعقبه أبو حيان قائلا : أن سيرتها وطريقتها ظرف مختص فلا يتعدى اليه الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r7.speaker: نحاة المغرب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r7.claim: Grammarians of the Maghrib classify derived nouns such as مذهب as an indefinite type of adverbial, without distinguishing those ending in tāʾ; on their analysis this accusative is neither anomalous nor forced.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r7.anchor: وفي شرح التسهيل عن نحاة المغرب انهم قسموا المبهم إلى أقسام منها المشتق من الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r8.speaker: الزمخشرى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī prefers parsing سنعيدها as complete on its own and سِيرَتَهَا as an absolute object of an understood verb: “we will restore it, moving in its former manner,” as when Moses leaned on it and used it for his flock.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p178/r8.anchor: وجوز الزمخشرى واستحسنه أن يكون ( سنعيدها ) مستقلا بنفسه غير متعلق بسيرتها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the Zamakhsharī parsing is good in meaning, with the implied participial clause either circumstantial or a new sentence, but it departs from the immediately apparent construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r1.anchor: والظاهر أنه جعل الجملة من الفعل المقدر وفاعله حالا ويجوز أن يكون استئنافا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r2.claim: The verse indicates that a thing may change its reality, as when a staff becomes a serpent; divine creative command can bring this about.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r2.anchor: والآية ظاهرة في جواز انقلاب الشئ عن حقيقته كانقلاب النحاس إلى الذهب وبه قال جمع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r3.claim: Some deny that a reality can turn into another, calling alteration of essences impossible and therefore outside the scope of divine power; al-Ālūsī rejects this denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r3.anchor: وقيل : لا يجوز لأن قلب الحقائق محال والقدرة لا تتعلق به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r4.claim: One account of transformation is that God creates gold in place of the copper; another, held by some theologians who regard atoms as alike in accepting attributes, removes copper’s property and creates gold’s property. The author favors the latter; only being copper and gold at once is impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p179/r4.anchor: يخلق بدل النحاس مثلا ذهبا على ماهو رأى بعض المحققين أو بأن يسلب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r6.claim: Al-Alūsī rejects the suggestion that Moses feared losing the staff's listed benefits, since it misjudges Moses' spiritual station.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r6.anchor: كان خوفه من فوات المنافع المعدودة ولذا علل النهى بقوله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r1.claim: Moses saw the staff as a fast-moving snake swallowing stones and trees, became afraid, and fled, so God told him to take it without fear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r1.anchor: فإنه لما رآها حية تسرع وتبتلع الحجر والشجر خاف وهرب منها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r2.claim: The phrase means its former form and state.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r3.claim: The accusative may follow an elided preposition, or the causative may derive from ʿāda, to return.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r3.anchor: وانتصابها على نزع الخافض أو على أن أعاد منقول من عاده بمعنى عاد إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r4.claim: Alternatively, it is adverbial: God will return it to its former way.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r4.anchor: أو على الظرف أي سنعيدها في طريقتها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r5.claim: Another parse estimates a verb: the staff will move as before and remain useful as before.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r5.anchor: أو على تقدير فعلها أي سنعيد العصا بعد ذهابها تسير سيرتها الأولى فتنتفع بها ما كنت تنتفع قبل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r6.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r6.claim: A report says Moses’ heart calmed, and he put his hand into the snake’s mouth and grasped its jaws.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:21/r6.anchor: قيل لما قال له ربه ذلك اطمأنت نفسه حتى أدخل يده في فمها وأخذ بلحييها

DURR-FULL:v5p564/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses fled; after first refusing to take the serpent, he was commanded again and then reassured that he was among the secure before taking it.
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {فألقاها فإذا هي حية تسعى}

DURR-FULL:v5p564/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses its former course as its former state.
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى} قال: حالتها الأولى

DURR-FULL:v5p564/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r10.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as its original appearance.
DURR-FULL:v5p564/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى} قال: هيئتها الأولى

BURSEVI:v5p289/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289/r1.claim: An unattributed Persian couplet counsels abandoning base worldly existence to find love’s alchemy and become gold.
BURSEVI:v5p289/r1.anchor: دست ازمس وجود ومردان ره بشوى تا كيمياى عشق بيابى وزر شوى

BURSEVI:v5p289/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289/r2.speaker: المولى الجامي
BURSEVI:v5p289/r2.claim: Jāmī says knowledge without action is poison and futile: one who knows alchemy has gained nothing unless he turns his own copper into gold.
BURSEVI:v5p289/r2.anchor: وقال المولى الجامي : وكسب علم كردى در عمل كوش

BURSEVI:v5p289/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289/r3.claim: Qāla is a resumption answering an implied question about what God did next.

BURSEVI:v5p289/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289/r4.claim: The staff became a male serpent that swallowed rocks and stones in its path, had eyes blazing like fire and loudly grinding fangs, and stretched forty or eighty cubits between its jaws; Moses fled from the terrifying sight.
BURSEVI:v5p289/r4.anchor: روي أنها انقلبت ثعبانا ذكرا يبتلع كل شيء يمر به من صخر وحجر وعيناه تتقدان كالنار

BURSEVI:v5p289/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289/r5.claim: Moses feared because fear and flight from snakes and similar creatures belong to ordinary human nature.
BURSEVI:v5p289/r5.anchor: لما رآه كذلك خاف ونفر لأن الخوف والهرب من الحيات ونحوها من طباع البشر

BURSEVI:v5p289/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289/r6.claim: Asked why Moses feared the staff while Abraham did not fear the fire, Bursevī says Abraham was more firmly established; God removed Moses’ initial fear, enabling him to take the staff and reach Abraham’s state of firmness.
BURSEVI:v5p289/r6.anchor: لأن الخليل كان أشد تمكينا إذ فرق بين بداية الحال ونهايتها وقد أزال الله هذا الخوف من موسى

BURSEVI:v5p289/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289/r7.claim: The Prophet likewise first feared Gabriel, then became ready to see him in his true form on the Miʿrāj, as described in 53:13–14.
BURSEVI:v5p289/r7.anchor: أول ما جاءه جبريل خافه فرجع من الجبل مرتعدا ثم كان من أمره ما كان

BURSEVI:v5p289/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p289/r8.claim: The inward reading says Moses first believed the staff held benefits, then feared its harm; taking it without fear teaches that God alone brings harm and benefit, so fear and hope belong to Him alone.
BURSEVI:v5p289/r8.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" {خذها ولا تخف} يعني كنت تحسب أن لك فيها المنافع

BURSEVI:v5p289/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289/r9.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v5p289/r9.claim: A Mathnawī couplet teaches that whoever fears God and adopts piety is feared by jinn and humans, while one who beholds God need fear no creature.
BURSEVI:v5p289/r9.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : هركه ترسيد از حق وتقوى كزيد

BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r1.claim: Sīra is a pattern or kind of going, figuratively a way or form; the accusative follows removal of a preposition and denotes the staff’s original shape.
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r1.anchor: السيرة فعلة من السير أي : نوع منه

BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r2.claim: Moses put his hand in the serpent’s mouth; it returned to a staff, with his hand in the familiar place between its forks. The sign prepared him not to fear its transformation before Pharaoh.
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r2.anchor: فوضع يده في فم الحية فصارت عصا كما كانت ويده في شعبتيها في الموضع الذي يضعها فيه

BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r3.claim: A hadith says that a person who failed to pay zakat will be brought with that wealth appearing as a serpent.
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث "يجاء لصاحب المال الذي لم يؤد زكاته بذلك المال على صورة ثعبان"

BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r4.claim: Every body, including a nonphysical one, has a spirit; each deed, trait, or attribute has a fitting form that becomes perceptible in the next life, as 6:108 says God will show people what they did.
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r4.anchor: لكل جسد روحا ولو كان معنويا ولكل عمل وخلق ووصف صورة معتدلة في الدنيا تتحو صورة محسوسة في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r5.claim: Love of wealth is a powerful trait of the commanding soul, which resembles a harmful serpent and becomes an alarming form around its owner’s neck when inner realities are exposed.
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r5.anchor: ولما كان حب المال من أشد صفات النفس الأمارة التي هي في صورة ثعبان ضار لا جرم يظهر يوم تبلى السرائر

BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r6.claim: When the heart is purified from love of wealth and comes to love spending in God’s way, that disposition takes a beautiful form suited to its good deeds; the same analogy applies to other traits.
BURSEVI:v5p289#2/r6.anchor: فإذا تزكى موسى القلب من حب المال وأحب بذله في سبيل الله جاء في صورة حسنة يهواها مناسبة لما عمل به من الخيرات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r1.claim: God told Moses to take the snake while it was still alive; when he placed his hand on it, it returned to being a staff.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r1.anchor: أمره باخذها وهي على حالها حية فوضع يده عليها فعادت عصا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ says sīratahā means its manner or condition: God will return it to how it was, a staff.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r2.anchor: قال الفراء طريقتها يقول تردها عصى كما كانت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says sīratahā is accusative after an omitted preposition, with the sense ‘return it to its former condition.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r3.anchor: وسيرتها منصوبة على اسقاط الخافض وافضاء الفعل اليها المعنى سنعيدها إلى سيرتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r4.claim: The description as a jān refers to the staff's initial state and as a great serpent to its final state; hayya can name either small or large snakes and either sex.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r4.anchor: فالجواب أن صفتها بالجان عبارة عن ابتداء حالها وبالثعبان اخبار عن انتهاء حالها والحية اسم يقع على الصغير والكبير والذكر والأنثى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj reconciles the descriptions by saying it had the body of a great serpent but the motion, speed, and lightness of a jān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p280/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج خلقها خلق الثعبان العظيم واهتزازها وحركتها وخفتها كاهتزاز الجان وخفته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r11.claim: God promises to restore the serpent to the staff's familiar original state.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p279/r11.anchor: ولهذا قال تعالى: {سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى} أي: إلى حالها

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r14.claim: One explanation says it was not a real dangerous snake but a sign of Moses' prophethood, so he should take it calmly; another says he was told to put his hand in its mouth, after which it became his staff again.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r14.anchor: يعني لم يكن قلبها حية للعقاب، وإنما كانت معجزة لنبوتك، فخذها آمنا مطمئنا ولا تخف أمرها

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r15.claim: The phrase means God will make the serpent a staff as before, or restore its former appearance.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r15.anchor: أي: نجعلها عصا كما كانت، وقيل: هيئتها الأولى

MUJAHID:v1p395#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p395#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p395#2/r1.claim: The phrase means God will restore the staff to its original form.
MUJAHID:v1p395#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى ﴾ يعني هيئتها الأولى

MUQATIL:20:19-23/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:19-23/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:19-23/r3.claim: God told Moses not to fear; when Moses grasped the serpent's tail, it returned to its original form as a staff.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r1.claim: Moses' fear had so subsided that he put his hand into the snake's mouth and took it by its jaws.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r1.anchor: بلغ من ذهاب خوفه أن أدخل يده في فمها وأخذ بلحييها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r2.claim: Sīra is the state a person is in, natural or acquired; it originally derives from a word for walking and came to mean condition or way. Here God returns the snake to its first state as a staff.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r2.anchor: والسيرة الحالة التي يكون عليها الانسان غريزية كانت أو مكتسبة وهي في الأصل فعلة من السير

NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r3.claim: Sīratahā is adverbial, meaning He will restore it to its first manner or condition, as it was when a staff.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r3.anchor: وانتصبت على الظرف أي سنعيدها في طريقتها الأولى أي في حال ما كانت عصا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r4.claim: God showed this to Moses during the conversation so he would not be frightened when the staff became a snake before Pharaoh.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53/r4.anchor: وأرى ذلك موسى عند المخاطبة لئلا يفزع منها إذا انقلبت حية عند فرعون

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r4.claim: God reassured Moses because the fear he felt was a natural human response.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r5.claim: A report says Moses first reached for the serpent through his robe sleeve, was told not to do that, then took it by hand and it returned to its original form.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r5.anchor: وروي أن موسى تناولها بكمي جبته فنهي عن ذلك، فأخذها بيده

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r6.claim: God showed this sign beforehand so Moses would not be frightened when he cast the staff before Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r6.anchor: وإنما أظهر له هذه الآية لئلا يفزع منها إذا ألقاها عند فرعون

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r7.claim: It was said that afterward the staff walked and conversed with Moses, carried loads, lit its prongs at night, became a bucket, and bore fruit.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r7.anchor: ويقال: إن العصا بعد ذلك كانت تماشيه وتحادثه ويعلق عليها أحماله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r8.claim: One account says the staff was made of myrtle from Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r8.anchor: وقيل: إنها كانت من آس الجنة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r9.claim: Another account says Gabriel brought the staff to Moses.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r10.claim: Another account says an angel brought the staff.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r10.anchor: وقيل: ملك. وقيل قال له شعيب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r11.claim: One account says Shuʿayb directed Moses to take a staff from a house; the one that fell to his hand was Adam's staff, brought down from Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r11.anchor: وقيل قال له شعيب: خذ عصا من ذلك البيت فوقعت بيده تلك العصا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r16.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r16.claim: Another account says Moses' fear vanished so completely that he put his hand into the serpent's mouth and seized its jaws.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r16.anchor: وقيل لما قال له ربه: «لا تخف» بلغ من ذهاب خوفه وطمأنينة نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r17.speaker: علي بن سليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r17.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān supplies an implied إلى before سيرتها, comparing the construction with اختيار موسى قومه.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r17.anchor: سمعت علي بن سليمان يقول: التقدير إلى سيرتها، مثل «واختار موسى قومه»

QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r18.speaker: علي بن سليمان
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r18.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān also allows سيرتها to be a verbal noun: سنعيدها means سنسيرها.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:19-22/r18.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا لأن معنى سنعيدها سنسيرها

QASHANI:20:19-21/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:19-21/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:19-21/r5.claim: Taking the staff means restoring it to intellectual control as before.
QASHANI:20:19-21/r5.anchor: أي: اضبطها بعقلك كما كانت { ولا تخف } من استيلائها عليك

QASHANI:20:19-21/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:19-21/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:19-21/r6.claim: Moses need not fear its domination or the variegation of his spiritual state: his anger has vanished, and the anger now moves by God's command, no longer hidden in the soul beneath heart-light.
QASHANI:20:19-21/r6.anchor: فإن غضبك قد فنى، فيكون متحركا بأمري وليس هو مستورا بنور القلب

QASHANI:20:19-21/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:19-21/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:19-21/r7.claim: Its first state is death and annihilation, reduced to vegetative capacity without awareness or impulse; it was called a staff because Moses' training under Shuʿayb made it like vegetative faculties, and Shuʿayb is said to have given it to him.
QASHANI:20:19-21/r7.anchor: أي: ميتة، فانية، صائرة إلى رتبة القوة النباتية التي لا شعور لها ولا داعية

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r5.claim: Moses’ fear can be explained as an instinctive reaction: he had never seen such a creature, and extreme panic can overwhelm rational knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r5.anchor: أن ذلك الخوف كان من نفرة الطبع لأنه عليه السلام ما شاهد مثل ذلك قط

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r6.speaker: أبو القاسم الأنصاري
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r6.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Anṣārī calls Moses’ fear strong evidence of his truthful prophethood, since a sorcerer knows his display is illusion and would not fear it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو القاسم الأنصاري رحمه الله تعالى وذلك الخوف من أقوى الدلائل

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r7.claim: Some say Moses feared the serpent because he knew what Adam had suffered from it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم : خافها لأنه عليه السلام عرف ما لقي آدم منها

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r8.claim: The command do not fear alone does not prove Moses was afraid, as do not obey the disbelievers does not prove obedience; his turning and fleeing in 27:10 does prove fear, which Razi contrasts with Muhammad’s freedom from worldly attachment.
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r8.anchor: مجرد قوله : { لا تخف } لا يدل على حصول الخوف

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r9.claim: A report says Moses put his hand between the serpent’s teeth and it became wood; the verse’s future wording means he took it after it had become a serpent.
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r9.anchor: روي أنه أدخل يده بين أسنانها فانقلبت خشبة والقرآن يدل عليه أيضا

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r10.claim: Taking the serpent safely and its return to wood are further miracles, strengthening the proof beyond the staff’s first transformation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r10.anchor: إدخال يده في فمها من غير ضرر معجزة وانقلابها خشبا معجز آخر فيكون فيه توالي المعجزات

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r11.claim: Razi regards the report that Moses took the serpent while still afraid as unlikely, since signs had accumulated and God had promised to restore it.

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r12.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r12.claim: Another view is that God’s command removed Moses’ fear and reassured him enough to take the serpent by its jaws.
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r12.anchor: وقال بعضهم لما قال له ربه : { لا تخف } بلغ من ذلك ذهاب خوفه

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r13.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r13.claim: Al-Kashshāf derives سيرة from السير, like ركبة from الركوب, then explains how it extended to mean a way or manner.
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r13.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : السيرة من السير كالركبة من الركوب

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r14.claim: One parsing treats سيرتها as منصوب after an omitted preposition, meaning سنعيدها إلى سيرتها.
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r14.anchor: أحدهما : بنزع الخافض يعني إلى سيرتها

RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r15.claim: Alternatively, سنعيدها stands independently: God will make the serpent a staff again, with سيرتها the object of an implied تسير, restoring its former uses.
RAZI-FULL:v22p25/r15.anchor: أن يكون سنعيدها مستقلا بنفسه غير متعلق بسيرتها بمعنى أنها كانت أولا عصا فصارت حية

QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r16.claim: The staff’s sequence of changes shows that God makes His servants stable through changing states, alternately gathering and separating them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r16.anchor: مرة عصا ثم ثعبانا ثم عصا مرة أخرى

STUDYQURAN:20:21/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r1.claim: Other accounts say Moses retreated when the staff became a serpent, without returning; the commentary points to these parallels.
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r1.anchor: Elsewhere in the Quran, when the staff becomes a serpent, Moses is said to have turned in retreat without returning

STUDYQURAN:20:21/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r2.claim: Some say Moses' fear subsided when God promised to restore the serpent to its former form, meaning the staff.
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r2.anchor: Some say that Moses’fear was assuaged when God informed him that He would cause the serpent to return to its former way

STUDYQURAN:20:21/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r3.speaker: other commentators
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r3.claim: Others say that after God said not to fear, tranquility and contentment came over Moses and ended his fear.
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r3.anchor: Yet others say that after God told Moses not to fear, a state of tranquility and contentment overcame him so that he was no longer fearful

STUDYQURAN:20:21/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r4.claim: Moses seized the serpent by its mouth, either at the teeth or jaw, and God turned it back into a wooden staff.
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r4.anchor: Moses then laid hold of the serpent by its mouth, grabbing it by either the teeth or the jaw

STUDYQURAN:20:21/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r5.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says God showed Moses the serpent beforehand so he would not fear when he later cast the staff before Pharaoh and his entourage.
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r5.anchor: Al-Qurṭubīexplains that God showed Moses the serpent as a way of preparing him

STUDYQURAN:20:21/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r6.speaker: philosophers and mystics
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r6.claim: They read the staff-serpent as the unrefined lower soul, which must be conquered for the soul's true nature to be realized.
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r6.anchor: Some philosophers and mystics read this verse as alluding to various aspects of the human being’s lower nature

STUDYQURAN:20:21/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r7.speaker: Mullā Ṣadrā
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r7.claim: Mullā Ṣadrā urges purifying and subduing the soul until it returns to its primordial disposition and lives intellectually, striving for the Return and Final Abode.
STUDYQURAN:20:21/r7.anchor: as explained by Mullā Ṣadrā: “There is no serpent like your soul; so slay it and purify it of the stain of its false beliefs

TAB-FULL:v16p47/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p47/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p47/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the serpent swallowed a tree and rock; Moses fled at the sound of the rock inside it, ignored two calls to take it, then took it after being assured he was safe.
TAB-FULL:v16p47/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: لما قيل لموسى: ألقها يا موسى، ألقاها {فإذا هي حية تسعى} [طه: 20]

TAB-FULL:v16p47/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p47/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v16p47/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says the serpent frightened Moses into fleeing, then God called to him not to fear, as stated in al-Naml.
TAB-FULL:v16p47/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: قال له، يعني لموسى ربه: {ألقها يا موسى} [طه: 19] يعني

TAB-FULL:v16p47/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p47/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p47/r4.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih describes a terrifying serpent with fangs in the form God willed; God told Moses to approach without fear and promised to restore it.
TAB-FULL:v16p47/r4.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، {قال ألقها يا موسى فألقاها فإذا هي حية تسعى} [طه: 20] تهتز، لها أنياب وهيئة كما شاء الله أن تكون

TAB-FULL:v16p48/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r1.claim: The object pronoun in khudh-hā refers to the serpent.
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r1.anchor: يقال لكل من كان على أمر فتركه، وتحول عنه ثم راجعه

TAB-FULL:v16p48/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r2.claim: God tells Moses not to fear the serpent.
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r2.anchor: يقال لكل من كان على أمر فتركه، وتحول عنه ثم راجعه

TAB-FULL:v16p48/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r3.claim: The serpent will return to its first form, a staff; Arabic uses this expression for resuming an earlier state after leaving it.
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r3.anchor: عاد فلان سيرته الأولى، وعاد لسيرته الأولى، وعاد إلى سيرته الأولى

TAB-FULL:v16p48/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as her first state.
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r4.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله {سيرتها الأولى} [طه: 21] يقول: حالتها الأولى

TAB-FULL:v16p48/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the phrase means her original form.
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {سيرتها الأولى} [طه: 21] قال: هيئتها

TAB-FULL:v16p48/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj transmits Mujāhid's gloss that the phrase means her original form.
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، مثله

TAB-FULL:v16p48/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r7.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r7.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says God would return it to a staff as before.
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r7.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن وهب بن منبه، {سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى} [طه: 21] أي سنردها عصا كما كانت

TAB-FULL:v16p48/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r8.claim: Qatāda glosses the promise as returning it to its first form.
TAB-FULL:v16p48/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، {سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى} [طه: 21] قال: إلى هيئتها الأولى

SULAMI:v1p440#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p440#2/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p440#2/r1.claim: Junayd says Moses' fear was fear of being overpowered by divine might, not an instinctive or natural fear.
SULAMI:v1p440#2/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : كان خوف موسى عليه السلام خوف تسليط

SULAMI:v1p440#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p440#2/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p440#2/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti says Moses saw on the staff a sign or covering of God's displeasure and punishment, so he did not feel safe from divine hidden power.
SULAMI:v1p440#2/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : خوف موسى من العصا أنه شاهد أثر

TABATABAI:20:18-21/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r9.claim: Sīra means a state or manner and originally denotes a kind or pattern of movement, just as jalsa denotes a kind of sitting.
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r9.anchor: السيرة الحالة والطريقة وهي في الأصل بناء نوع من السير كجلسة لنوع من الجلوس

TABATABAI:20:21-22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r1.claim: The command to take the staff back and the reassurance imply that Moses feared what he saw; 28:31 says he fled and did not turn back.
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r1.anchor: فيه دلالة على خوفه عليه السلام مما شاهده من حية ساعية وقد قصه تعالى في موضع آخر إذ قال فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان

TABATABAI:20:21-22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r2.claim: The first condition to which God will restore the snake is its original state as a staff.
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r2.anchor: أي حالتها { الأولى } وهي أنها عصا

TABATABAI:20:21-22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r3.claim: Khawf is taking precautions against harm; khashya is inner agitation and disturbance of the heart.
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r3.anchor: والخوف وهو الأخذ بمقدمات التحرز عن الشر غير الخشية التي هي تأثر القلب واضطرابه

TABATABAI:20:21-22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r4.claim: Prophets may experience ordinary fear but not khashya understood as a blameworthy weakness incompatible with courage; 33:39 says messengers fear none but God.
TABATABAI:20:21-22/r4.anchor: فإن الخشية رذيلة تنافى فضيلة الشجاعة بخلاف الخوف والأنبياء عليهم السلام يجوز عليهم الخوف دون الخشية

TABRISI:20:20-23/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:20-23/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:20-23/r6.claim: Sīratahā is accusative with an understood preposition: “We will return it to its original state.”
TABRISI:20:20-23/r6.anchor: وسيرتها انتصب على تقدير سنعيدها إلى سيرتها فحذف الجار

FARRA:v2p176/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p176/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p176/r7.claim: سيرتها الأولى means its former way or shape: the staff is returned to what it was.
FARRA:v2p176/r7.anchor: أي طريقتها الأولى. يقول: يردها عصا كما كانت.

THALABI:v1p86/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p86/r1.claim: An Arab expression fasartu al-farasa means driving a horse until its hair or covering is worn away; this is offered as an etymology for tafsīr.
THALABI:v1p86/r1.anchor: هو من قول العرب: فسرت الفرس إذا ركضتها مصورة لينطلق حصيرها

THALABI:v1p86/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p86/r2.claim: Arabs also say fasartu al-nāqata for driving a camel until its hair falls away and its skin appears.
THALABI:v1p86/r2.anchor: تقول العرب: فسرت الناقة، إذا سيرتها حتى زال شعرها، وظهر جلدها

THALABI:v1p86/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r3.speaker: بعض الهذليين
THALABI:v1p86/r3.claim: A verse by an unnamed Hudhali poet is cited for the camel usage, but its wording is omitted in this excerpt.
THALABI:v1p86/r3.anchor: ظهر جلدها. وأنشدوا فيه لبعض الهذليين

THALABI:v1p86/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p86/r4.claim: Tafsīr means uncovering the closed meaning of an expression and releasing what is held back from understanding.
THALABI:v1p86/r4.anchor: فيكون معنى التفسير: كشف المنغلق من المراد بلفظه وإطلاق المحتبس عن فهمه

THALABI:v1p86/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p86/r5.claim: Taʾwīl makes the initial meaning a general sense consistent with what precedes and follows; its root points to return, as in saying “I turned it and it turned back.”
THALABI:v1p86/r5.anchor: والتأويل: بكون الأول معنى مجمله موافق لما قبلها وما بعدها، وأصله من الأول، وهو من الرجوع

THALABI:v1p86/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p86/r6.claim: The Arabic expression awwaltuhu means “I redirected it,” and it turned back.
THALABI:v1p86/r6.anchor: تقول العرب: أولته. قال: أي صرفته فانصرف

THALABI:v1p86/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r7.speaker: النضر
THALABI:v1p86/r7.claim: Al-Nadr derives taʾwīl from iyāla, governance: Arabs say that they governed and were governed, so an interpreter manages speech and places its meaning correctly.
THALABI:v1p86/r7.anchor: عن جده النضر أنه قال: «أصله من الإيالة، وهي السياسة، تقول العرب: قد ألنا، وإيل علينا، أي سسنا، وساسنا غيرنا

THALABI:v1p86/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p86/r8.claim: The two terms are built on the tafʿīl pattern because it conveys repetition, like tracing one sūra after another and one verse after another.
THALABI:v1p86/r8.anchor: وإنما بنوهما على التفعيل لأنه يدل على التكثير، وكأنه تتبع سورة بعد سورة وآية بعد آية

THALABI:v1p86/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r9.speaker: العلماء
THALABI:v1p86/r9.claim: Scholars define tafsīr as knowledge of a verse's revelation, circumstances, story, and causes of revelation.
THALABI:v1p86/r9.anchor: قالت العلماء: التفسير: علم نزول الآية وشأنها وقصتها، والأسباب التي نزلت فيها

THALABI:v1p86/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r10.speaker: العلماء
THALABI:v1p86/r10.claim: Scholars say people may not speak about revelation circumstances and causes except on the basis of transmitted reports.
THALABI:v1p86/r10.anchor: فهذا وأضرابه [محظورة] على الناس القول إلا باستماع الأثر

THALABI:v1p86/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r11.speaker: العلماء
THALABI:v1p86/r11.claim: Taʾwīl is less restricted because it turns a verse toward a meaning the wording can bear, which scholars may infer.
THALABI:v1p86/r11.anchor: فأما التأويل فالأمر فيه أسهل لأنه صرف الآية إلى معنى يحتمله

THALABI:v1p86/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p86/r12.speaker: العلماء
THALABI:v1p86/r12.claim: The measure for interpretive inference is the Qurʾan and Sunna.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278#2/r1.claim: God will restore the transformed object to being a staff as it was before.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p278#2/r1.anchor: سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى} أي: نردها عصا كما كانت.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r1.claim: God displayed the sign to prepare Moses for the miracles he would show Pharaoh, so he would not panic or flee when the staff became a serpent; this verse implies fear although al-Qasas mentions it explicitly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r1.anchor: وذلك أن الله تعالى أراد أن يري موسى ما أعطاه من الآيات التي لا يقدر عليها مخلوق؛ لئلا يفزع منها إذا ألقاها عند فرعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r2.speaker: عطاء والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r2.claim: ʿAta and al-Suddi say God will return it to being a staff as before.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r2.anchor: قال عطاء والسدي: (نردها عصا كما كانت)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses sīrataha as its state or condition.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses sīrataha as its form or appearance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses sīrataha as its original creation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r6.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad says it means God will make the staff as it had been.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r7.claim: The meaning is that the staff will resume its former behavior and condition as a staff.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r7.anchor: والمعنى في الآية: أنها تجري على ما كانت تجري عليه من قبل، من كونها عصا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r8.claim: Abu Ishaq says sīra means form or condition and is accusative because the preposition ilā has been omitted from the construction “return it to its former state.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r8.anchor: ونحو هذا قال أبو إسحاق في السيرة: (أنها الهيئة، يقال إذا كان القوم مشتبهين: هم على سيرة واحدة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq analyzes sīrataha as accusative after deletion of ilā, with the verb extending directly to its object.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r9.anchor: قال: و {سيرتها} منصوبة على إسقاط الخافض، وأفضى الفعل إليها، والمعنى: إلى سيرتها، فلما حذفت (إلى) أفضى الفعل، وهو {سنعيدها}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r10.speaker: وهب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r10.claim: Wahb reports that Moses covered his hand with his cloak before grasping the serpent; an angel asked whether the cloak could protect him if God allowed his fear, and Moses admitted it could not but said he was created weak. He then grasped it and found his familiar staff and hand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p382#3/r10.anchor: قال وهب: (لما أمره الله بأخذها أدنى طرف المدرعة (7) على يده، فقال له ملك: أرأيت يا موسى لو أذن الله بما تحاذر، أكانت المدرعة تغني عنك شيئا؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r8.speaker: قتادة وابن مجاهد عن أبيه
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r8.claim: Qatadah and Ibn Mujahid, quoting his father, explain that God would restore the staff to its first form.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r8.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة وابن مجاهد، عن أبيه قالا: أي على هيئتها الأولى: عصا

MAJAZ:v2p17/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p17/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p17/r3.claim: Sīratahā al-ūlā means the form it had before; the verb may also take ilā when someone returns to a former way, as Abū Zayd says.
MAJAZ:v2p17/r3.anchor: سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى» (21) أي خلقتها التي كانت عليها قبل ذلك وقد يجعلون أيضا بينها وبين الذي قبلها «إلى»

BURHAN:v3p215/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p215/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p215/r3.claim: We will return it to its former course means to its former course, with ʿalā understood before sīrata.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r1.claim: The construction illustrated by the opening example is usually heavy, but when it avoids affectation it becomes delicate and witty.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r1.anchor: ولا شبهة في ثقل ذلك في الأكثر ، ولكنه إذا سلم من الاستكراه لطف وملح .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r2.claim: Ibn al-Mu'tazz, al-Khalidi, Abu Tammam, and al-Mutanabbi supply examples whose beauty comes from carefully composed phrasing.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r2.anchor: خذها ابنة الفكر المهذب في الدجى والليل أسود رقعة الجلباب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r3.claim: The metaphor of being bound by someone's kindness is commonplace even in ordinary speech; its poetic beauty comes from the path taken in composition.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p95/r3.anchor: الاستعارة في أصلها مبتذلة معروفة ؛ فإنك ترى العامي يقول للرجل يكثر إحسانه إليه وبره له

TABRISI:20:21-28/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:21-28/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:21-28/r1.claim: One account describes an enormous serpent crossing rock like a pregnant camel, swallowing it, uprooting a great tree with its fangs, fire in its eyes, and the staff's crook becoming a meteor-haired neck; Moses fled, then stopped from shame before God and returned when called, still terrified.

TABRISI:20:21-28/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:21-28/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:21-28/r2.claim: God tells Moses to take the serpent with his right hand without fear and promises to return it to its original state as a staff.

TABRISI:20:21-28/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:21-28/r3.speaker: وهب
TABRISI:20:21-28/r3.claim: Wahb says Moses wore a wool garment and initially covered his hand with its edge; God asked whether the garment could protect him if God allowed the danger. Moses admitted his weakness, uncovered his hand, and put it in the serpent's mouth, where it returned to its familiar place between the staff's prongs.
TABRISI:20:21-28/r3.anchor: وعلى موسى يومئذ مدرعة من صوف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:21-26/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:21-26/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:21-26/r1.claim: God will return the staff to its former state as a staff.

ITQAN:v2p320/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p320/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p320/r3.claim: Sīra means its condition or former state.

NAHHAS:v3p36/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p36/r2.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v3p36/r2.claim: Ali ibn Sulayman parses سيرتها with an understood إلى, comparing the construction to واختار موسى قومه.
NAHHAS:v3p36/r2.anchor: سمعت علي بن سليمان يقول التقدير إلى سيرتها

NAHHAS:v3p36/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p36/r3.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v3p36/r3.claim: Ali ibn Sulayman also allows سيرتها to be a verbal noun because سنعيدها means سنسيرها.
NAHHAS:v3p36/r3.anchor: قال ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا لأن معنى سنعيدها سنسيرها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r1.claim: Moses is told to take the staff in his right hand and not fear: God will restore it to its original form.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r1.anchor: {قال خذها} بيمينك، {ولا تخف سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى} هيئتها الأولى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r2.claim: One account says Moses wore a wool cloak fastened with twigs and covered his hand with its end; God ordered him to uncover it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r2.anchor: وكان على موسى مدرعة من صوف قد خلها بعيدان، فلما قال الله تعالى: خذها، لف طرف المدرعة على يده، فأمره الله تعالى أن يكشف يده فكشف.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r3.claim: Another account has an angel ask whether Moses' cloak could protect him if God allowed what he feared; Moses says no, but admits his weakness, then reaches into the serpent's mouth and recovers the staff.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r3.anchor: وذكر بعضهم: أنه لما لف كم المدرعة على يده قال له ملك: أرأيت لو أذن الله بما تحاذره أكانت المدرعة تغني عنك شيئا؟ قال: لا ولكني ضعيف، ومن ضعف خلقت،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r4.speaker: قال المفسرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r4.claim: The signs were shown to Moses so he would see a miracle beyond human ability and would not panic when casting the staff before Pharaoh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون: أراد الله عز وجل أن يري موسى ما أعطاه من الآية التي لا يقدر عليها مخلوق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270#2/r1.claim: Sīratahā is accusative with the preposition ilā omitted; the sense is to its former state.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {سيرتها الأولى} نصب بحذف "إلى"، يريد: إلى سيرتها الأولى.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r11.claim: Moses naturally feared the serpent, and God’s command to take it was training him for what he would face before Pharaoh.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r11.anchor: اي الله تبارك وتعالى على ما يكون منها عند فرعون لأجل التدريب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r12.claim: Sīra means way or state; God promises to restore the serpent to its former state as a staff, a promise that cannot fail.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r12.anchor: أي بعظمتنا عند أخذك لها بوعد لا خلف فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r13.claim: The sign confirms that the speaker is the Lord with the most beautiful names; Moses becomes calm, puts his hand in the serpent’s mouth, takes its beard, and finds his hand between the staff’s prongs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r13.anchor: وبلغ من طمأنينته أن أدخل يده في فمها وأخذ بلحيتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r2.claim: Moses felt the fear natural to human beings; a report says he first reached for the staff with his sleeves, then took it by hand when told to.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه أوجس في نفسه خيفة أي لحقه ما يلحق البشر، وروي أن موسى تناولها بكمي جبته فنهي عن ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r3.claim: When Moses grasped it by hand, the serpent became a staff again in its original state.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r3.anchor: فأخذها بيده فصارت عصا كما كانت أول مرة وهي سيرتها الأولى

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r6.claim: Iʿāda means returning something a second time to its original state.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r6.anchor: والإعادة: رد الشيء ثانية على ما كان عليه أولا

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r7.claim: Sīra and ṭarīqa are near-synonyms; sīra evokes an object's passage or movement in a direction.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r7.anchor: والسيرة والطريقة من النظائر، والسيرة: مرور الشيء في جهة، سار يسير سيرة حسنة

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r11.claim: Sīratahā is accusative either as the direct object of sanʿīduhā or after an omitted preposition, ilā.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r11.anchor: انتصب سيرتها قيل: بوقوع الفعل عليها وهو قوله: سنعيدها، وقيل: بنزع الخافض تقديره: إلى سيرتها
